Raw mass is V, probability MA is raw/V, and E(phi+c)=E(phi)+c. Finite dual energy is equivalent to integrability of every E1 potential. notes.text:
Primary-source partial theorem. Retain k algebraically closed, trivially valued and characteristic zero, X reduced irreducible projective of dimension n, and omega an ample real numerical Cartier class, including c1(L) for every ample line bundle. Set V=(omega^n)>0. BJ1801.08229v4 permits nonnormal varieties in its conventions and general varieties in Section 7. Theorem12.8 assumes irreducibility, whereas the sufficient envelope theorem5.20 assumes smoothness and connectedness.

Configurations are integrally closed in their prescribed generic fiber. Absolute normalization would change a nonnormal X. BJ1.13 gives vertical DVRs. For a central component E write b_E=ord_E(t), v_E=b_E^(-1)ord_E. The genuine mixed raw model measure is sum_E b_E product_i((omega_i,model+D_i)|E) delta_vE. Relative nefness gives nonnegative weights; the central-fiber intersection cycle gives mass (omega_1...omega_n).

Compactified intersection extends by decreasing model majorants and is finite on mixed E1 tuples. BJ7.18 defines its Radon measure by integral h M=pairing((0,h),(omega_1,phi_1),...,(omega_n,phi_n)) for genuine model-PL tests. Positivity bounds the functional by mass times sup norm; PL density and Radon representation supply its unique extension. BJ7.19 proves actual model agreement, mass, mixed integrability, decreasing continuity and normalization pushforward. Weighted continuity7.21 uses the pairing containing the test minus the pairing containing zero. This constructs the genuine operator before equation surjectivity.

The actual energy is E(phi)=pairing((omega,phi)^(n+1))/((n+1)V), with E(0)=0 and E(phi+c)=E(phi)+c. E1 consists of genuine global psh potentials with E>−infinity. Raw diagonal MA has mass V; probability MA=raw/V. Model locality and weighted continuity give the winning potential's measure on its strict winning locus. Equal masses give integral_{phi<psi} MA(psi)<=integral_{phi<psi} MA(phi). With I=integral (phi-psi)(MA(psi)-MA(phi)), mixed estimates give I>=0. Equal measures imply I=0; finite-dual-energy divisorial Dirac tests and minimal usc divisorial extension give equality after equal-sup normalization. Thus uniqueness is modulo one real constant. Global domination10.6 also precedes EP and applies to genuine global potentials.

For a positive Radon raw target nu its mass must be V. Put mu=nu/V. The exact finite-dual-energy condition is sup_{psi in E1}(E(psi)-integral psi mu)<infinity. BJ9.20 proves equivalence with integrability of every E1 potential. A bounded-J weighted-sum argument rules out unbounded target integrals: a decreasing sum of normalized psi_j with J bounded and integrals <=−2^j would have finite energy but integral −infinity. The mixed expansion I(t psi,0)<=t[1-(1-t)^n]I(psi,0)<=n t^2 I(psi,0) supplies the scaling estimate. Necessity for actual MA targets follows from the energy tangent inequality. This characterization alone does not assert solvability.

Under genuine EP, general BJ5.11 supplies normalized-PSH compactness. Uniform two-sided energy differentiation8.5, bounded-J target L1 convergence9.19 and energy usc give variational attainment. Approximation of the target by maximizing model measures9.11 precedes attainment. Testing both f and −f forces the constructed genuine MA measure to equal mu. The raw objective is VE−integral phi nu; mass V gives translation invariance. Target completeness and the MA embedding give strong E1 completeness after surjectivity. Conversely completeness of bounded increasing model maxima supplies envelopes. This is the general-variety EP/surjectivity equivalence12.8, not an unconditional singular theorem. Dimension zero is the separate constant one-point case.

notes.summary: Relative tropical supports give curve subharmonicity and radial trace equality without ambient convex extension or arbitrary-H(s) affine regularization. Actual FS tests fix slicing weights before selecting a weak witness.
notes.detailedSummary: The curve proof checks common skeletal lisse membership, zeros and identically-zero coordinates, type I/IV neighborhoods, real breakpoints, positive outgoing slopes and decreasing stability. The radial proof checks the nontrivial complete algebraically closed extension, exact Wanner scope, disk comparison, ramification, properness, Artinian dimensions and minus-infinity cases. Determinant traces satisfy the actual affine FS generator/floor condition. The preceding smooth weak open-trace extension remains an explicit antecedent.
notes.text:
Independent curve and algebra proof drafts. Correct Wu2609.27610v1's relative contact condition to f(t')>=ell(t')+C with equality at t, retaining its finite affine convention. This auxiliary correction does not redefine the genuine global PSH problem. On a smooth curve over complete algebraically closed nontrivially valued Omega of residue characteristic zero, a finite continuous PL selection in regular log-norm coordinates with these relative supports is subharmonic.

At infinite coordinates, finite affine expressions have zero coefficient on a smaller chart; identically-zero pulled coordinates are discarded. Remaining coordinates are units. Thuillier2.2.24 factors their logs through a common semistable skeleton, and2.3.20 makes them harmonic. Along subdivided edges the coordinates are affine. A continuous finite affine selection switches only at finitely many intersections, so the pullback is lisse, including real breakpoints. Unit-log germs are locally constant at type I/IV points by2.3.21. At an interior skeleton point subtract the pulled-back harmonic contact support H. Every outgoing slope of b−H is nonnegative, while the harmonic weighted slope sum vanishes. Thus the lisse Laplacian coefficient is sum_e w_e slope_e(b−H)>=0. Wanner2.11/Thuillier3.4.4 gives subharmonicity; Thuillier3.1.8(ii) passes decreasing limits, including the identically −infinity alternative.

No ambient convex extension is inferred. On the union of rays (1,0),(0,1),(1,1), values 0,0,t have relative local supports but cannot extend convexly near the origin: convexity would force the midpoint value <=0. This example distinguishes the assertions without purporting to be a balanced tropicalization.

For any complete residue-characteristic-zero F, extend to Omega. For trivial F first use F((T)), |T|=e^−1, then its completed algebraic closure; otherwise use the completed algebraic closure of F. Wanner's standing field is complete, algebraically closed and nontrivially valued. Section4 additionally fixes a smooth proper algebraic curve. When invoking4.3 or4.7, compactify by a normal projective function-field model and apply only on the original open. The slope proof itself uses Section2 and Thuillier.

Disk comparison gives h(center)<=h(boundary Gauss). Usc and convergence of those Gauss points to the rational center give the reverse limiting inequality, including a −infinity center. This is a radial boundary limit, not an ordinary punctured-neighborhood limit. Locally a finite curve map has t=c z^e U(z), U(0)=1. Residue characteristic zero permits an analytic e-th root of U, giving t=c y^e after an invertible coordinate change. A small target Gauss point has one source Gauss point per disk, with actual fiber dimension e: after scaling, Y^e=alpha T is Eisenstein over the residue rational-function field. The center's Artinian length is also e. Finite properness excludes other preimages nearby. Radial limits establish the weighted center equality. If one summand tends to −infinity, usc bounds the others above, so no subtraction of infinities occurs.

Artinian trace base change is proved independently for every pulled-back function. Tensor each original local factor with the new completed residue field. Refined dimensions sum to its original dimension and refined finite residue norms restrict to its original point. The weighted identity therefore needs no regularizable-function antecedent.

For reduced finite locally free B/A of rank d and actual affine FS u=max(lambda,c_i log|f_i|+C_i), clear coefficients with integer D. Set b0=1, bi=f_i^(D c_i), w0=D lambda and wi=D C_i. The basis-independent determinant P(T)=det(mult_(sum T_i bi))=sum a_beta T^beta lies in A[T]. Artinian composition series give P=product_x(sum T_i bi(x))^length_x after algebraically closed extension. Weighted Gauss norms are multiplicative at every positive real polyradius: lexicographically largest maximal terms give a unique maximal product contribution. Scalar extension preserves coefficient norms. Hence N(u)=max_beta(D^−1 log|a_beta|+D^−1 sum beta_i wi), with rational floor d lambda.

The determinant coefficients need not generate A. Polynomial degree bounds expressing base generators g_j in source generators give u>=eta_j log|g_j compose pi|−M_j. Adding dominated branches d eta_j log|g_j|−dM_j leaves the trace unchanged and supplies the actual base-algebra generator condition. Supplied decreasing sequences trace termwise; generic finiteness of their limit remains separate. Dini is used only for finite continuous limits. For a=z^2 and u=max(log|z|,−1), P=T0^2−aT1^2 gives N(u)=max(−2,log|a|); the center has one nilpotent factor of dimension two, not an unweighted point.

For finite integral Y->S with S affine open in A^n over the retained k, generic norm coefficients extend because they are integral over normal A[T] and lie in K[T]. Normalize a line preimage through the H(s)-rational lift, generically in an etale open. Height bounds and finiteness make its components curves; normalization gives smooth finite-flat curves of total degree d. Radial equality for global FS tests gives identical weighted sums for every line/open. Differences of actual FS functions form a rational lattice, contain constants and separate the finite analytic fiber by truncated log norms with dominated generator branches. Their finite-set closure contains every function, so each slicing weight is fixed. At nonflat fibers these are normalized slicing weights, not necessarily original fiber-algebra dimensions.

For a weak input, choose the line after shrinking the open where its proper birational witness is an isomorphism. Properness extends the generic lift across normalized-curve DVRs. The curve theorem identifies a previously constructed globally regularizable open-trace extension with the fixed weighted trace everywhere. The weights were fixed before this input-specific choice. This repairs Wu6.12 Step3's boundary equality, but does not construct the preceding trace extension or smooth weak upper-growth base. A cusp-product example still produces nondiscrete H(s) internally in the original projective unibranch domain; no stronger arbitrary-H(s) affine regularization theorem is inferred.

notes.detailedSummary: Using n1, BJ2.12/2.33 supply a bounded genuine ample model potential with positive actual mass at each source-convention divisorial point. notes.text:
Using n1's genuine global operator, the model-atom argument removes a Dirac-equation premise. BJ2.12 realizes every source-convention divisorial x as a Rees valuation on a flag-ideal configuration closed integrally in its prescribed generic fiber. BJ2.33 puts an ample test bundle on this same model. On its central component E, (L_model|E)^n>0 and b_E>0; the actual raw weight b_E(L_model|E)^n is therefore positive at x. The resulting potential is bounded and genuine globally psh, also for nonnormal X. This uses neither EP nor equation surjectivity. Source divisorial points are rationally scaled; no atom at every arbitrary real scaled point is asserted.

If bounded local potentials have compatible mixed positive measures, exact mass V, comparison and divisorial determination, translate this test b below phi and set phi_t=(1−t)phi+t b. Under phi<=psi MA(psi)-a.e., comparison gives full MA(phi_t) mass to {phi_t<psi}. Mixed positivity gives an atom >=t^n MA(b) at x, forcing phi_t(x)<psi(x). Let t->0 and use divisorial determination. These local antecedents are not supplied by the atom. With them, known smooth EP and contact orthogonality would globalize bounded local potentials using a decreasing directed net of continuous majorants on compact Hausdorff analytification. A sequence is not assumed over uncountable k.

For a global algebraic affine FS expression a=max(lambda,q_j log|f_j|+A_j), write f_j=F_j/s0^d_j on an embedding compactification with exhaustion g=−log||s0||_theta>=0. If a−cg<=C on R<=g<=R+1, set G=min(g,R+1), H_j=max(log||F_j||_(d_j theta),−M_j). Choose rational thresholds so −q_jM_j+(q_jd_j−c)G+A_j<=C throughout [0,R+1]. Clipped section norms are differences of actual basepoint-free FS metrics. BJ's rational PL space is a vector lattice; its real span need not be.

Set A*=max(C,lambda−cG,{q_jH_j+(q_jd_j−c)G+A_j}), choose rational K>0 with C+K>=sup A*, and F*=min(A*,C+K(R+1−G)). For g<=R the cap is inactive; on the shell A*=C; for g>=R+1, including the entire divisor, the cap is C. Thus the collar has genuine algebraic model-PL representation. It does not identify arbitrary analytic PL with model PL. These explicit local maxima have positive curvature. Flag-ideal formulas give actual pullback over k((t)) at every analytic point. CLD18.8.6 preserves positivity;18.8.4 on residual central curves gives nonnegative degree. The represented model is nef and enters genuine PSH by the n1 criterion.

A common compact shell works for an entire tail of an already supplied decreasing global FS sequence: nested closed superlevel sets supply the collar, without Dini to a singular limit. Genuine decreasing closure and complete-system restriction give the legitimate already-regularizable extension. Hartogs coefficients max_{j,i>=1}(log|f_j,i|−c_j)/i have this algebraic form when the Hartogs domain is already Runge. Adding epsilon_r g−r supplies generators and a floor. This does not prove an arbitrary weak-input Hartogs domain is Runge.

The entropy simplex dual of chi(x)=a^−1 log(1+sum exp(a x_i)) has rational finite face-respecting polyhedral approximants with uniform error on the whole extended tropical space. Rational intercepts and vertex branches retain floors and generators; error shifts make them decreasing. Positive rational series use upper partial sums plus an exhaustion tail. For a real support C+sum alpha_i log|f_i|, choose log|f_i|<=d_i v, rational q_i,m increasing to alpha_i>0, B_m decreasing from above to sum d_i alpha_i, and C_m decreasing to C. Set b_m=B_m−sum d_iq_i,m>0. Then max(C_m+sum q_i,m log|f_i|+b_m v,epsilon_m v−m) decreases globally, including poles, retaining generator/floor branches. Relative entropy and compact gap sublevels give strict separation outside every contact neighborhood. These actual global FS supports use no singular envelope.

For localization in integral nonnormal affine R, assume a log|h|+b<=max(u,−c log|f|)+O(1), h in R_f, and |log|f||<=M on L union {x}, where x is in the original R-polynomial hull. Divisorial rays on the finite normalization force a max(−ord_Dh,0)<=c ord_Df. For q/p>c/a, z=h^pf^q is integral over R and lies in R_f. One f^N kills R[z]/R, so z^ell f^N belongs to R for every ell. The original hull inequality, followed by ell->infinity and q/p decreasing to c/a, gives a log|h(x)|+b<=sup_L(a log|h|+b)+2cM, including zero endpoints. This repairs false denominator counting for f=z^2,g=z. The full regularizable maximum principle still needs controlled approximants.

Under finite harmonic charts refined by test coordinates, Green's formula gives corner coefficient sum_sigma w_sigma partial_(inward transverse)b. Subtract a harmonic contact support: tangential terms cancel and transverse derivatives are nonnegative. Harmonic balancing removes the support. The sign agrees with the positive outgoing-slope Laplacian of |x|. Strongly positive facet tests have nonnegative density; collapsed facets vanish only in the refined chart. Application to every relative-image PL input still needs finite rational-domain representation. CLD17.8.4 states strict integer PL, whereas18.8.8 prints integer PL and cites it; this distinction remains explicit. The narrower GM route requires properness over nontrivial k((t)), strict domains and rational constants cleared after tensoring, followed by residual nefness and BJ's smooth-only4.19. CLD8.7.2 does not handle merely decreasing bounded discontinuous limits.

The common-reference bookkeeping is verified: theta=omega+ddc p, negative FS floor, h=A v+M+1 and Psi=max(u−h,0) require Phi=Psi/A+p and G=v−p+(M+1)/A, giving Phi+G=u/A. Once genuine common representations exist, BJ weighted decreasing continuity constructs local products and overlaps. Full intrinsic products, partition/integration-by-parts, exact mass and comparison remain unreconstructed. Arbitrary Rossi and split analytic-piece gluing are not covered by the algebraic collar. For z->z^2, a split-piece indicator has continuous trace two on a disk about zero and one on a disjoint disk about one; actual dimensions are retained when fibers stay unsplit. Thus gamma must be localized. At gamma=1 there is no other positive weight in that piece and no division by gamma−1. These repairs do not prove the complete Runge induction.

notes.text:
The original P16.1 target and completion criteria remain unchanged and unproved. Retain every reduced irreducible geometrically unibranch projective variety over every algebraically closed trivially valued characteristic-zero field, in every dimension, and every ample line bundle. n1 also supplies the genuine global partial theory for ample real numerical Cartier classes. n2 closes the relative-support curve positivity and radial trace equality obligation with its preceding open-trace extension still an antecedent. n3 supplies model atoms and algebraic inputs, while recording remaining gates. No unrelated equation axis is inferred.

The concrete remaining obligations are: (1) finite rational-domain representation and calibrated chart application for the full higher-dimensional corrected local class, resolving strictness; (2) complete smooth bounded-local mixed products, integration by parts, exact mass/comparison and genuine common representation, followed by smooth weak and controlled principal-open extension; (3) arbitrary analytic Rossi/split-piece gluing and the full local-projection/Hartogs/Runge induction; (4) the countable rational singular envelope base, hence singular EP, arbitrary-cardinality/real-class passage, unconditional variational existence and onto normalization. Current positivity and radial equality cannot construct these antecedents.

Normalization q of a geometrically unibranch X is finite birational degree one, with singleton geometric fibers and unchanged residue fields in characteristic zero. Analytification is a homeomorphism. Unconditionally E(q*phi)=E(phi), volume is unchanged and q_* genuine mixed MA(q*phi_i)=genuine mixed MA(phi_i), by projection formula and decreasing pairings. Onto PSH separately requires BJ5.13's approaching larger classes with EP. Onto E1, equal dual energies and full operator/target correspondence follow under that antecedent. They are not proved here without it. The conditional cardinality passage descends finite data to countable algebraically closed subfields, preserves relative closure via vertical R1/S2 and regular extension, checks components/multiplicities/degrees, and uses genuine mixed pushforward, contact orthogonality and BJ global domination. Real classes require actual class closure from above. Neither passage supplies the missing base.

The nodal obstruction is unconditional. Let C be a rational irreducible projective nodal curve with normalization P1 and distinct node preimages p1,p2. Put d=deg L>0 and v=ord_p1. The downstairs delta_v has finite dual energy. Blow up P1 times A1 at (p1,0). The model p*(q*L)+d X0−d E has central degrees 0,d and multiplicities one, so it is nef and has genuine raw measure d delta_v. Its potential is d max(1−s,0) on the p1 ray and d on other rays, with endpoint values 0,d. A downstairs E1 solution would pull up with the same target by genuine pushforward, positivity, fixed mass and the singleton lift of the function-field valuation. Upstairs uniqueness forces this potential plus a constant, while a downstairs pullback must have equal endpoint values. Contradiction: an actual finite-dual-energy target is nonsolvable outside unibranchness.
